findings.title: Do not bypass installer verification when the integration is missing
findings.body: When no Integration row exists for the supplied installation_id, this branch advances the pipeline without checking the authenticated GitHub user against the installer. build_integration then retrieves that installation using app credentials, which does not establish that the OAuth user has access to it. A user who supplies another installation's ID before its installation webhook has created the Integration row can therefore attach it to their Sentry organization. The missing-row path needs to fail closed or independently verify ownership rather than skipping the new security check.

findings.title: Handle integrations without sender metadata
findings.body: The new check unconditionally indexes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"], but sender is optional in build_integration, and the basic installation flow in this file's tests explicitly creates metadata without it. If such an Integration remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed, attempting to attach it again now raises KeyError and returns a server error instead of completing or displaying the invalid-installation message. Handle missing sender metadata explicitly and obtain trustworthy installer information if it is required.

findings.title: Compare immutable GitHub user IDs instead of logins
findings.body: The ownership check compares the current OAuth user's login with the login stored in the installation webhook. GitHub usernames can be changed and subsequently claimed by another account, so these strings do not reliably identify the same user. After the installer renames their account, the legitimate installer is rejected, while a different account claiming the old username can pass verification for an unlinked installation. Store and compare the immutable GitHub user ID from both responses instead.
